labels.name: Arachidonic acid
labels.function: Membrane fatty acid that is the substrate NSAIDs keep from conversion

labels.name: Cyclooxygenase (COX-1/COX-2)
labels.function: Blocked by NSAIDs; celecoxib selectively blocks the type 2 isoform

labels.name: Prostaglandins
labels.function: Sensitize pain endings; their loss causes GI ulcers and kidney injury

labels.name: Nociceptor
labels.function: Peripheral pain-sensing ending activated by tissue injury

labels.name: Mu opioid receptor
labels.function: Morphine's principal target; naloxone reverses its activation

labels.name: Gi/o protein
labels.function: Inhibitory transducer coupling opioid binding to effectors

labels.name: Adenylyl cyclase
labels.function: Enzyme whose activity falls after opioid receptor activation

labels.name: Voltage-gated calcium channel
labels.function: Closes with opioids, so less transmitter is released into the cleft

labels.name: Potassium channel
labels.function: Opens with opioids, hyperpolarizing the second-order neuron

labels.name: Brainstem
labels.function: Site where cyclobenzaprine reduces tonic motor activity

labels.name: Excitatory presynaptic terminal
labels.function: Drives motor neurons; its overactivity underlies spasticity

labels.name: Alpha-2 adrenergic receptor
labels.function: Tizanidine's target; ciprofloxacin (CYP1A2 block) raises drug levels

labels.name: GABA-B receptor
labels.function: Baclofen's target; renally cleared drug accumulates in CKD

labels.name: Spinal motor neuron
labels.function: Final cell that sets muscle tone; quieted by central agents

labels.name: Sarcoplasmic reticulum
labels.function: Intracellular calcium store for excitation-contraction coupling

labels.name: Ryanodine receptor (RyR1)
labels.function: Dantrolene blocks its calcium release; treats malignant hyperthermia

diagrams.title: Adverse-effect organ map for MSK pain drugs (schematic)

labels.name: Brainstem respiratory center
labels.function: Opioid toxicity here slows breathing; give naloxone

labels.name: Pupil
labels.function: Pinpoint in opioid toxicity

labels.name: Airways
labels.function: Bronchospasm in aspirin-sensitive patients given NSAIDs

labels.name: Heart
labels.function: Nonaspirin NSAIDs raise MI risk; avoid cyclobenzaprine in arrhythmia

labels.name: Liver
labels.function: Acetaminophen excess injures it; N-acetylcysteine is the antidote

labels.name: Stomach
labels.function: NSAID prostaglandin loss causes ulceration and bleeding

labels.name: Kidney
labels.function: NSAIDs reduce its perfusion; baclofen accumulates when it fails

labels.name: Colon
labels.function: Opioid constipation, the effect with little tolerance

labels.name: Bladder
labels.function: Retention from anticholinergic relaxants or opioids
